trust_decision.summary: Accept as the published, already-fixed advisory for ts-deepmerge: merge() writes caller-controlled keys into a fresh result object, and before the fix a key naming an Object.prototype method (toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty, ...) became an own property of the merged output, so a later coercion or method call throws an uncaught TypeError (CWE-248). The fix at 305a058 extends the existing key blocklist at src/index.ts:64 to a curated UNSAFE_KEYS set; I treat that guard as the protected sink and stay inside this repo at the pinned commit.

landing_point.why: The only unsafe-key defence in the library is the inline blocklist `["__proto__", "constructor", "prototype"].includes(key)` inside the merge loop; an engineer reading the advisory summary greps for the existing blocklist and extends exactly this line.

fix_sites.entry_point: merge(...objects) (src/index.ts:51) and merge.withOptions(options, ...objects) (src/index.ts:127, which delegates to merge)
fix_sites.module_kind: library source, public API core merge loop

fix_sites.entry_point: module-level constant consumed by merge()/merge.withOptions(); the new UNSAFE_KEYS set lands between `};` at line 45 and `interface IObject` at line 47

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The guard must stay a silent skip, not a rejection: merging an object that carries a blocked key has to succeed and still return the object's intended data. The pinned test merges JSON.parse('{ "__proto__": { "hasProto": true } }') and expects a normal return object, so a fix that throws, or that rejects/strips the whole input object on seeing an unsafe key, breaks the library's documented permissive merge. The neighbouring permissive cases (an array-like `length` key merging normally at src/index.test.ts:208-210, Date values passing through) sit next to it.

O6_input_shapes: keys delivered as own data properties via JSON.parse, e.g. { "__proto__": ... } (already blocked at the pinned commit)
new method names toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty, isPrototypeOf, propertyIsEnumerable, toLocaleString, independent of the value type (object or primitive)
the same names at any nesting depth of plain objects, because nested objects are re-entered through the recursive merge call (src/index.ts:76-79)
pre-existing names constructor and prototype (already blocked)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A recursive sanitisation of object elements held inside arrays (merge never descends into array items, so { list: [{ toString: 1 }] } passes through untouched).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Arrays of config objects are a normal input, and the mergeArrays branch already walks every element to dedupe/concatenate, so a maintainer hardening 'the merged output must not contain prototype-shadowing objects' would plausibly add the same key filter there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The options defaults/merge route `merge.options = { ...defaultOptions, ...options }` in withOptions, which builds an object from caller-supplied keys with no filter.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the second place in the file that constructs an object out of caller keys, so extracting a shared sanitising helper and routing both merges through it is a natural refactor.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second exported entry point written alongside withOptions, e.g. merge.into(target, ...sources) / an assign-style lower-level API that writes keys straight into a caller-provided target.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: In-place merge into an existing target is the most common feature request for a merge library, and it would need the same blocklist at its own write site.

O9_family: prototype method override written into merged output, producing an uncaught exception on later coercion/call (CWE-248)

O10_build.language: TypeScript (ESM package, dual ESM/CJS output; only src/ is checked in at the pinned commit)
O10_build.toolchain: Node >=14.13.1, yarn, tsc via tsconfig.esm.json/tsconfig.cjs.json, jest + ts-jest with NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules, eslint + prettier
O10_build.project_tests: src/index.test.ts — one jest suite covering merge semantics, arrays, options and reported issues, including the prototype-pollution regression at src/index.test.ts:220-227; the fix commit adds or changes no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add just the one key named in the report's example (typically "toString") to the existing includes() array at src/index.ts:64, leaving the rest of the Object.prototype method names open.

out_of_scope_notes: Noticed but not pursued, outside this advisory: merge.withOptions mutates the module-global merge.options and only restores it on the success path (src/index.ts:131-138), so a merge that throws leaves the global options altered — a separate robustness issue, not the method-override flaw.
